data.title: Acrochordon (skin tag) — viva
data.summary: Benign tumours & cysts · 9 viva questions with answers
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Acrochordon (skin tag)** (Benign tumours & cysts)_

**Q1. What is an acrochordon?**
- Common benign soft fibroepithelial polyp (skin tag, soft fibroma) — small, soft, skin-coloured or pigmented, pedunculated papules on neck, axillae, groin, eyelids, inframammary; middle age, obese, pregnant women

**Q2. Associations.**
- Obesity, insulin resistance/type 2 diabetes, metabolic syndrome, acanthosis nigricans, dyslipidaemia, pregnancy (hormonal), acromegaly, PCOS; Birt–Hogg–Dubé (fibrofolliculomas mistaken for tags), Cowden; association with colonic polyps is debated

**Q3. Histopathology.**
- Polypoid lesion with loose fibrovascular stroma (collagen and dilated vessels), thin overlying epidermis (may be acanthotic/papillomatous), no adnexa; fat in larger lesions (fibrolipoma)

**Q4. Differential diagnosis.**
- Pedunculated seborrhoeic keratosis, intradermal naevus, neurofibroma (button-hole sign), molluscum, filiform wart, fibroepithelioma of Pinkus, pedunculated BCC/melanoma (rare — remove and send if atypical), fibrofolliculomas (BHD)

**Q5. Treatment.**
- Snip excision with sterile scissors (with or without local anaesthetic) and haemostasis, cryotherapy, radiofrequency/electrocautery, ligation for larger ones; send atypical lesions for histopathology
- Screen for diabetes/metabolic syndrome in patients with multiple tags (especially with AN)

**Q6. What is Birt–Hogg–Dubé syndrome?**
- Autosomal dominant FLCN mutation: multiple fibrofolliculomas, trichodiscomas and acrochordons on face/neck, lung cysts with spontaneous pneumothorax, renal tumours (chromophobe/oncocytic) — screen kidneys with MRI

**Q7. Can skin tags be a marker of systemic disease?**
- Multiple skin tags associated with insulin resistance/type 2 diabetes, obesity, metabolic syndrome, acanthosis nigricans, dyslipidaemia, pregnancy (hormonal), and possibly colonic polyps (controversial); check fasting sugar, lipids in multiple tags

**Q8. What causes a skin tag to become painful and dark?**
- Torsion of the stalk with infarction — black, tender, may auto-amputate; differentiate from a thrombosed haemangioma or melanoma (biopsy if doubtful)

**Q9. Dermoscopy of a skin tag.**
- Pedunculated lesion with central or 'comma'/hairpin vessels and skin-coloured/light-brown structureless areas; cerebriform features if seborrhoeic keratosis-like

## Quick spotter facts
- Multiple soft pedunculated neck papules with AN — skin tags; check sugar

_Sources: Previous-year PG question papers (Sahana P Raju, Solved Papers Dermatology); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e (Benign fibrous tumours). Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
